attempts.label: DANDI:001702
attempts.paper_title: Degradation of perineuronal nets in hippocampal CA2 explains the loss of social cognition memory in Alzheimer's disease
attempts.entry_title: CA2 perineuronal nets and social memory in 5XFAD mice (Chaunsali et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Most of this paper's main findings cannot be tested in this dataset, and the RNA-seq results that can be tested only partly hold. The dandiset's NWB files hold no images or measurements, and the behaviour videos have no labels or scored times, so the PNN loss in CA2 and the social memory deficits and their rescue could not be tested. In the RNA-seq counts from GEO, the 7 month immune upregulation and the PNN-gene and remodeling-gene directions held. The 3 month gene counts and learning and memory terms depend on undescribed DESeq2 and enrichment choices. At 7 months the 314 up genes held (284 to 320), but the 6 down genes did not (0 to 7). The ECM term claim rests on one marginal reading.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Chaunsali, Li, Fleischel et al. (2025) on dandiset 001702. The dandiset's NWB files hold only metadata, with no images or measurements, and its behaviour videos carry no subject, group or trial labels, so the immunohistochemistry and behaviour claims are blocked. The bulk RNA-seq claims of Figure 4 are tested on the counts the authors deposited in GEO (GSE317499), with pydeseq2 and a pinned Gene Ontology release.

The four readings give different outcomes. With independent filtering at alpha 0.1, one model per age, unshrunken, gives 95 up and 136 down, both within tolerance (reproduced); one model on all 16 samples, unshrunken, gives 51 and 141, the down count within tolerance and more down than up (partially reproduced); shrunken fold changes give 88 and 45 (separate) and 39 and 37 (joint), which meet neither the full nor the partial criterion. Filtering at pydeseq2's alpha 0.05 changes only the separate model's counts, to 98 and 137 unshrunken and 91 and 45 shrunken, and gives the same outcome under every reading. The paper names only DESeq2 1.44.0 (Methods 2.5). Question for the paper's authors (finding methods_unavailable): which DESeq2 design gave Figure 4B, and were the fold changes shrunken? The match of the separate unshrunken reading suggests that design, but an outcome cannot be chosen by its match.
deviations: The counts are GEO GSE317499 (GSE317499_counts.csv.gz, read and checked against its SHA-256), not data in the dandiset; 4 mice per age and genotype, from GEO, as the paper does not give n.

DESeq2 1.44.0 in R is replaced by pydeseq2 0.5.4 (Python), with DESeq2's defaults (Cooks refit, independent filtering, Benjamini-Hochberg); independent filtering is tuned at alpha 0.1, the default of R's results(), set explicitly as pydeseq2's default is 0.05. Its shrinkage is pydeseq2's apeglm-type prior. R cannot be pinned in the entry's locked environment, and the counts were not compared with R.

The Methods name only DESeq2 1.44.0 (Methods 2.5), so the four readings of the criterion are run, (a) or (b) model with (c) or (d) fold changes, and the outcome is the one they all give, by the claims file's READINGS rule.

outcomes.notes: The 16 readings give different outcomes. In 15 no term naming extracellular matrix organization, assembly, disassembly or secretion reaches adjusted p < 0.05 in either 7 M contrast (not reproduced). In one (separate model, shrunken, all annotated genes, no size limit) extracellular matrix organization reaches 0.048 in 7 M against 3 M 5XFAD (partially reproduced). With the 10 to 500 limit alone all 8 readings give not reproduced, so the outcome rests on running the term-size limit as a reading (see deviations). The deciding value is marginal: the term holds 6 of the 224 DEGs (p 0.018, rank 1183 of 3171 terms tested), and with one DEG fewer its adjusted p would be 0.113. It also rests on pydeseq2's shrinkage standing in for R's apeglm, not compared with R, and on the GO release. With release 2024-01-17 the same reading gives 0.046 and the same outcomes per reading; with release 2025-03-16 it gives 0.052 and all 16 readings give not reproduced. In 7 M 5XFAD against control the smallest ECM-term adjusted p under any reading is 0.061 (0.059 to 0.065 over the three releases). The 3 M contrast has none under any reading (smallest 0.145), as the claim says. Under the joint unshrunken reading the 7 M ECM terms hold 5 DEGs, all up. Asked of a reader (questions/001702.yaml): the Figure 4F and 4G legend ranks the top 10 PNN and ECM terms by adjusted p but does not say they were significant, so the criterion's adjusted p < 0.05 may be stricter than the paper.

findings.statement: None of the 481 NWB files holds data. Each is 185,480 bytes and holds only file-level metadata (identifier, session description, keywords, subject); acquisition, processing, analysis and stimulus are empty. The identifiers name the original image files of Figures 1, 3, 5 and S1 to S6 and S9, but no image, ROI, table or measurement is deposited, although the description says the dandiset includes immunohistochemical imaging data quantifying PNN integrity. All 22 IHC claims of the paper are blocked.

The 175 behaviour videos are MP4 files outside NWB, named only by figure panel and trial number. They carry no subject, genotype, treatment, DPI or trial-type (Novel 1, Familiar, Novel 2; familiarization or test) label, several arenas share each video, and the counts do not match the paper's mice (for example 15 videos for the 16 mice of Figure 2B, 33 for the 26 of Figure 5E). The scored interaction and exploration times are not deposited. None of the 19 behaviour claims can be tested.

The object recognition videos are deposited four times, under Fig 2I, Fig 2J, Fig 2K and Sup Fig 7 (byte-identical by SHA-256), and in each set Trial 6 and Trial 7 are the same file: 28 assets hold 6 distinct recordings.

The description says the dandiset includes bulk RNA-sequencing data with associated metadata; it holds none, and the counts are in GEO GSE317499 only. The description also keeps a placeholder sentence naming GEO accession "GSEXXXXX" next to the one naming GSE317499.

The NWB subject is a group label, not an animal (82 subject_ids for 481 files, up to 31 files sharing one, such as 5xFAD+_6M_Fig1), so slices cannot be grouped by mouse, which the paper's per-mouse tests (Figure 5I) and five mice per group (Figure 1) need. Sex is U in 476 of 481 files, and session descriptions give the region as Unknown.

Question for the paper's authors: which DESeq2 design gave the DEG counts of Figure 4B and 4C (one model per age, or one model on all 16 samples with contrasts), and were fold changes shrunken before the |log2FC| > 1 cut? One model per age reproduces 95 and 136 at 3 M (98 and 137 with independent filtering at 0.05 in place of R's 0.1); one model on all samples gives 51 and 141. And which enrichment tool, background, term-size limits and GO release gave Figures 4D to 4G? The number of learning and memory terms in the 3 M top 10 is 0 to 3 depending on these choices, and an ECM term reaches adjusted p < 0.05 in one of 16 readings. Three claims are blocked on these choices.

In GEO GSE317499, sample GSM9473154 (3 Month, 5xFAD negative, rep2) has library name 20790 while its run name carries 20690; the count matrix column (M3_5xFAD-10) matches it by sample number, age and genotype.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive API and tested the helper's DEG, enrichment, z-score and term-pattern functions on synthetic inputs. It gave its own outcome for each claim. Its other points: the GEO library name 20790 of GSM9473154 against run name 20690 (already a finding), and the background (a) and Cauchy-prior shrinkage choices, which it found reasonable; neither changed anything. It also noted that the fig4c down-count tolerance of 0.6 requires exactly 6 genes, a point about the claims file, which is not changed.

disagreements.reason: The four readings disagree (cell 13). (a)(c) gives 98 up / 137 down, both within tolerance, so reproduced. (b)(c) gives 51/143, so partially reproduced. (a)(d) gives 91/45 and (b)(d) 38/37: more up than down, so not reproduced. Cell 10 says (b)(c) is adopted where the readings disagree; that is the author's own rule, and the claims file's READINGS rule makes a claim methods_underspecified when readings disagree (problem 1). pydeseq2's DeseqStats defaults to alpha 0.05 for independent filtering where R results() defaults to 0.1 (problem 2).

With the 10 to 500 term-size limit, the top 10 hold 3/3, 0/0, 2/2 and 1/1 memory terms with negative z for (a)(c), (a)(d), (b)(c) and (b)(d) across the two backgrounds. That spans reproduced, not reproduced and partial. With no size limit the count is 0 under every reading (cell 19). GO_MIN, GO_MAX = 10, 500 is the author's assumption, not a reading in the claims file (problem 3).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 51 outcomes. Its other points: no outcome is marked assumed; the round-1 reasons in the record reproduce its round-1 text and outcomes faithfully, and the reviewed paragraph summarises its remaining points correctly but omits the fig4c tolerance point; the comparison with R DESeq2 is still not done, and it cannot change fig4b, fig4d or fig4c but can change fig4fg.

entries.name: 001702-chaunsali-2025
entries.title: CA2 perineuronal nets and social memory in 5XFAD mice (Chaunsali et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Chaunsali, Li, Fleischel et al. (2025) on dandiset 001702. The dandiset's NWB files hold only metadata, with no images or measurements, and its behaviour videos carry no subject, group or trial labels, so the immunohistochemistry and behaviour claims are blocked. The bulk RNA-seq claims of Figure 4 are tested on the counts the authors deposited in GEO (GSE317499), with pydeseq2 and a pinned Gene Ontology release.
